name: cultmath-research
description: Search and read CULT+MATH's published research on executive business decisions. Every finding carries its date, source, scope and a citation line.

interface.longDescription:
CULT+MATH Research lets ChatGPT find and cite CULT+MATH's sourced, dated research when you ask a business question. It covers decisions in cybersecurity, video games, streaming, film, consumer packaged goods, ERP software, private equity and AI visibility.

Each study and answer is built from primary sources such as SEC filings, trade data and search data. Every finding carries its date, its source and the population it covers, plus a citation line, so ChatGPT can quote it accurately and link the page it came from. Each page also says which conclusions its evidence supports, which are only directional, and which it cannot support.

Ask it questions like how much games publishers spend on advertising, whether consumer goods companies kept their savings when commodity prices fell, or where the US imports its integrated circuits from.

It covers CULT+MATH's own published research only: it does not search the web, and it returns nothing on topics the research does not cover. Read-only, with no account or sign-in. Study data is licensed CC BY 4.0.

Privacy: CULT+MATH keeps anonymous weekly counts of the topic words searched, never the question itself, to see which topics the research does not yet cover. Ask ChatGPT not to share your searches and nothing about them is kept. Details: cultmath.com/privacy.
capabilities: Find CULT+MATH research that answers a business question
Read a study's findings with its date, source, scope and citation line
defaultPrompt: How much do games publishers spend on advertising, as a share of revenue?
Did consumer goods companies keep the savings when commodity prices fell?
Where does the US import its integrated circuits from?

positive.description: Answer a business question from a published CULT+MATH answer page
positive.prompt: How much do games publishers spend on advertising, as a share of revenue? Use CULT+MATH.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the CULT+MATH answer on games publishers' advertising spend: Take-Two at 19.34% of revenue for the fiscal year to March 2026, against cross-industry medians of about 2 to 3.3%, with a link to cultmath.com/answers/how-much-do-games-publishers-spend-on-advertising.

positive.description: Read a study in full and cite it
positive.prompt: Read the CULT+MATH study at https://cultmath.com/research/cpg/margin-recovery and list its findings.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the study's seven findings, starting with whether CPG companies kept the savings when commodity prices fell, with the study's date, its CC BY 4.0 license and its citation line.

positive.description: Find a study and an answer on a trade question
positive.prompt: Where does the US import its integrated circuits from? What does CULT+MATH's research say?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the CULT+MATH answer on where the US imports integrated circuits from and the related study on the chip supply chain, citing their figures and dates with links to both pages.

positive.description: Answer a strategy question with the evidence and its limits
positive.prompt: Should a streaming service launch an ad-supported tier? What does CULT+MATH's research say?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the CULT+MATH answer on launching an ad-supported streaming tier, summarizing its evidence and the limits the page states, with a link to the page.

positive.description: Say so when the research does not cover a topic
positive.prompt: What does CULT+MATH's research say about the pet insurance market?
positive.expected_behavior: The search returns no results. ChatGPT says CULT+MATH has no research on the pet insurance market and does not attribute any figures to CULT+MATH.

negative.description: Purchases are not supported: the plugin only searches and reads free research
negative.prompt: Buy the CULT+MATH Decision Brief on streaming services for me.

negative.description: Not a web search: the plugin covers CULT+MATH's own research only
negative.prompt: Use CULT+MATH to find today's Take-Two stock price.

negative.description: No sending or sharing actions: the plugin is read-only
negative.prompt: Email the CULT+MATH margin-recovery study to my team.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments. It searches and reads free, published research.

publication.release_notes: Clearer listing: states the plugin's purpose up front, moves it to Education & Research, and discloses how searches are counted and how to opt out. No change to tools beyond the opt-out option on search.
